Data Centers Face Scrutiny Over Water Use and Chemical Concerns

A new report indicates that data centers are increasingly using per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), often called 'forever chemicals,' to manage heat, a practice that raises environmental concerns. These chemicals are being used as a coolant, and major producers of PFAS are reportedly expanding output to meet demand from the artificial intelligence sector. This trend coincides with growing backlash against data centers, leading some political figures to implement new regulations. For instance, one governor has drawn a line on data center development, while in the Senate, legislative roadblocks have spurred new competition over data center bills. The long-term viability of current data center investments is also being questioned, with predictions that trillions of dollars could become obsolete within years.
